author: foundedceo
caption:
Most founders spend all of their time building products while very few spend enough time building the legal foundation that protects everything they’re creating. Documents like NDA, SAFE, LOI, MSA, SOW, DPA, and BAA may not help you land your first customer, but they often determine whether your company survives long enough to become a great one. Many startups fail because ownership is unclear, IP isn’t properly assigned, contracts were never signed, or legal problems emerge as the company begins to scale.

Investors can help improve products, refine strategy, and even replace leadership. What they can’t fix is a company built on weak legal infrastructure. As your startup grows, every hire, advisor, contractor, customer, investor, and fundraising round introduces new legal complexity. The strongest founders understand that building a company is also about protecting what you’re building from day one.

author: chatgptricks
caption:
Harvard and MIT built 8.3 billion AI personas.

The project is called MatrAIx, a simulation system designed to test digital products on simulated users before real people ever see them. Its Persona 8B database contains 8.3 billion profiles, each described across 1,290 traits covering everything from demographics to preferences and behavior.

These simulated users can take surveys, interact with AI assistants, browse websites, and use apps. Researchers ran 18,189 evaluation trials, including a controlled study where the personas followed their assigned behavioral traits 91.5 percent of the time.

The team has also released about 1 million personas publicly on Hugging Face, while the code is available on GitHub under an MIT license.

This could give companies a new way to test how different types of people might react to a product before launching it.

Would you trust simulated users to predict real ones?
Source: MatrAIx / arXiv

caption:
Comment "CLAUDE" to get this AI tool to run Claude Code for free and with unlimited usage.

You can now run Claude Code for completely free, with almost unlimited usage.

Someone on GitHub just built a free tool called OmniRoute.

It links your Claude Code to over 200 free AI providers.

The moment your Claude limit runs out, it automatically switches you to the next best model.

So your session keeps going without any interruption.

Think of it like a relay race.

When one runner gets tired, the next one picks up the baton without breaking stride.

Plus it compresses your prompts before they even reach the model.

This cuts your token usage by up to 90%, while keeping the same output quality.

That's the part most routing tools get wrong. They save you money on rate limits but still burn through tokens fast.

OmniRoute attacks both problems at once.

It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and basically every AI coding tool out there.

One config file, and your entire setup runs on free models.

Setup takes minutes. Just one npm install, and you're routing through 200+ providers instantly.

For developers tired of hitting daily limits mid-project, this changes how much you can actually build in a day.
